passages.text: In those days Hezekiah became mortally ill. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Put your house in order, for you are about to die; you will not recover.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah became very sick.
Hezekiah was about to die.
Isaiah was a prophet.
Isaiah was the son of Amoz.
Isaiah came to Hezekiah.
Isaiah spoke to Hezekiah.
Isaiah said, “This is what the LORD says.”
The LORD said, “Put your house in order.”
The LORD said, “You are going to die.”
The LORD said, “You will not recover.”
passages.original: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם חָלָ֥ה חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ לָמ֑וּת וַיָּב֣וֹא אֵ֠לָיו יְשַׁעְיָ֨הוּ בֶן־ אָמ֜וֹץ הַנָּבִ֗יא וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ צַ֣ו לְבֵיתֶ֔ךָ כִּ֛י מֵ֥ת אַתָּ֖ה וְלֹ֥א תִֽחְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD, saying, “Please, O LORD, remember how I have walked before You faithfully and with wholehearted devotion; I have done what was good in Your sight.” And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
He became very sick.
Hezekiah turned his face to the wall.
Hezekiah prayed to the LORD.
Hezekiah said, “Please, O LORD, remember me.
I have walked before You faithfully.
I have served You with a whole heart.
I have done what is good in Your sight.”
Hezekiah wept with great sorrow.
passages.original: וַיַּסֵּ֧ב חִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ פָּנָ֖יו אֶל־ הַקִּ֑יר וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֖ל אֶל־ יְהוָֽה׃ וַיֹּאמַ֗ר אָנָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ זְכָר־ נָ֞א אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁ֧ר הִתְהַלַּ֣כְתִּי לְפָנֶ֗יךָ בֶּֽאֱמֶת֙ וּבְלֵ֣ב שָׁלֵ֔ם וְהַטּ֥וֹב בְּעֵינֶ֖יךָ עָשִׂ֑יתִי וַיֵּ֥בְךְּ חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ בְּכִ֥י גָדֽוֹל׃ס

passages.text: And the word of the LORD came to Isaiah, saying, “Go and tell Hezekiah that this is what the LORD, the God of your father David, says: ‘I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears. Behold, I will add fifteen years to your life.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Isaiah.
The LORD gave Isaiah a message.
The LORD told Isaiah to go to Hezekiah.
The LORD is the God of David, Hezekiah’s ancestor.
The LORD said, “I have heard your prayer, Hezekiah.
I have seen your tears.
I will add fifteen years to your life.”
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר־ יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל־ יְשַׁעְיָ֖הוּ לֵאמֹֽר׃ הָל֞וֹךְ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֶל־ חִזְקִיָּ֗הוּ כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵי֙ דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֔יךָ שָׁמַ֙עְתִּי֙ אֶת־ תְּפִלָּתֶ֔ךָ רָאִ֖יתִי אֶת־ דִּמְעָתֶ֑ךָ הִנְנִי֙ יוֹסִ֣ף עַל־ יָמֶ֔יךָ חֲמֵ֥שׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֖ה שָׁנָֽה׃

passages.text: And I will deliver you and this city from the hand of the king of Assyria. I will defend this city.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Hezekiah through Isaiah.
The LORD is the God of David, Hezekiah’s ancestor.
The LORD said He would save Hezekiah.
The LORD said He would save the city of Jerusalem.
The LORD said He would rescue them from the king of Assyria.
The LORD said He would protect the city.
passages.original: וּמִכַּ֤ף מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁוּר֙ אַצִּ֣ילְךָ֔ וְאֵ֖ת הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֑את וְגַנּוֹתִ֖י עַל־ הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּֽאת׃

passages.text: This will be a sign to you from the LORD that He will do what He has promised: I will make the sun’s shadow that falls on the stairway of Ahaz go back ten steps.’ ” So the sunlight went back the ten steps it had descended.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Isaiah.
The LORD is the God of David, Hezekiah’s father.
The LORD gave a sign to Hezekiah.
The LORD promised to do what He said.
The LORD said, “I will make the shadow move back.”
The shadow was on the stairway of Ahaz.
The shadow had gone down ten steps.
The LORD made the shadow go back ten steps.
The sunlight went back the ten steps it had descended.
passages.original: וְזֶה־ לְּךָ֥ הָא֖וֹת מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֙ יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֵּֽר׃ הִנְנִ֣י מֵשִׁ֣יב אֶת־ צֵ֣ל הַֽמַּעֲל֡וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָרְדָה֩ בְמַעֲל֨וֹת אָחָ֥ז בַּשֶּׁ֛מֶשׁ אֲחֹרַנִּ֖ית עֶ֣שֶׂר מַעֲל֑וֹת וַתָּ֤שָׁב הַשֶּׁ֙מֶשׁ֙ עֶ֣שֶׂר מַעֲל֔וֹת בַּֽמַּעֲל֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָרָֽדָה׃ס

passages.text: This is a writing by Hezekiah king of Judah after his illness and recovery: I said, “In the prime of my life I must go through the gates of Sheol and be deprived of the remainder of my years.”
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
He became very sick.
He recovered from his illness.
Hezekiah wrote these words after he was healed.
Hezekiah said, “I am in the prime of my life.
I must go through the gates of Sheol.
I will lose the rest of my years.”
passages.original: מִכְתָּ֖ב לְחִזְקִיָּ֣הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָ֑ה בַּחֲלֹת֕וֹ וַיְחִ֖י מֵחָלְיֽוֹ׃ אֲנִ֣י אָמַ֗רְתִּי בִּדְמִ֥י יָמַ֛י אֵלֵ֖כָה בְּשַׁעֲרֵ֣י שְׁא֑וֹל פֻּקַּ֖דְתִּי יֶ֥תֶר שְׁנוֹתָֽי׃

passages.text: I said, “I will never again see the LORD, even the LORD, in the land of the living; I will no longer look on mankind with those who dwell in this world.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
He became very sick.
He recovered from his illness.
Hezekiah spoke about his feelings.
He said, "I will never see the LORD again in the land of the living."
He said, "I will not look on the LORD while I am alive."
He said, "I will not see people anymore."
He said, "I will not be with those who live in this world."
passages.original: אָמַ֙רְתִּי֙ לֹא־ אֶרְאֶ֣ה יָ֔הּ יָ֖הּ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ הַחַיִּ֑ים לֹא־ אַבִּ֥יט אָדָ֛ם ע֖וֹד עִם־ י֥וֹשְׁבֵי חָֽדֶל׃

passages.text: My dwelling has been picked up and removed from me like a shepherd’s tent. I have rolled up my life like a weaver; He cuts me off from the loom; from day until night You make an end of me.
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
He became very sick.
He recovered from his illness.
Hezekiah wrote about his experience.
He said his home was taken away from him.
His home was removed like a shepherd’s tent.
Hezekiah compared his life to a weaver’s work.
He rolled up his life like a weaver rolls up cloth.
God cut him off from life, like a weaver cuts cloth from the loom.
From morning until night, God brought him to an end.
passages.original: דּוֹרִ֗י נִסַּ֧ע וְנִגְלָ֛ה מִנִּ֖י כְּאֹ֣הֶל רֹעִ֑י קִפַּ֨דְתִּי כָאֹרֵ֤ג חַיַּי֙ מִדַּלָּ֣ה יְבַצְּעֵ֔נִי מִיּ֥וֹם עַד־ לַ֖יְלָה תַּשְׁלִימֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: I composed myself until the morning. Like a lion He breaks all my bones; from day until night You make an end of me.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is suffering and in distress.
I stayed calm until the morning.
God acts with great power.
He breaks all my bones like a lion.
From day until night, You bring me to an end.
passages.original: שִׁוִּ֤יתִי עַד־ בֹּ֙קֶר֙ כָּֽאֲרִ֔י כֵּ֥ן יְשַׁבֵּ֖ר כָּל־ עַצְמוֹתָ֑י מִיּ֥וֹם עַד־ לַ֖יְלָה תַּשְׁלִימֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: I chirp like a swallow or crane; I moan like a dove. My eyes grow weak as I look upward. O Lord, I am oppressed; be my security.”
passages.sermon:
The speaker is suffering and calls out to God.
I make sounds like a swallow.
I make sounds like a crane.
I moan like a dove.
My eyes become weak as I look up to heaven.
Lord, I am oppressed.
Be my security.
passages.original: כְּס֤וּס עָגוּר֙ כֵּ֣ן אֲצַפְצֵ֔ף אֶהְגֶּ֖ה כַּיּוֹנָ֑ה דַּלּ֤וּ עֵינַי֙ לַמָּר֔וֹם אֲדֹנָ֖י עָֽשְׁקָה־ לִּ֥י עָרְבֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: What can I say? He has spoken to me, and He Himself has done this. I will walk slowly all my years because of the anguish of my soul.
passages.sermon:
I do not know what to say.
God has spoken to me.
God has done this.
I will walk slowly all my years.
My soul feels deep anguish.
passages.original: מָֽה־ אֲדַבֵּ֥ר וְאָֽמַר־ לִ֖י וְה֣וּא עָשָׂ֑ה אֶדַּדֶּ֥ה כָל־ שְׁנוֹתַ֖י עַל־ מַ֥ר נַפְשִֽׁי׃

passages.text: O Lord, by such things men live, and in all of them my spirit finds life. You have restored me to health and have let me live.
passages.sermon:
The Lord gives life to people through these things.
My spirit finds life in all of them.
You, Lord, have healed me.
You have let me live.
passages.original: אֲדֹנָ֖י עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם יִֽחְי֑וּ וּלְכָל־ בָּהֶן֙ חַיֵּ֣י רוּחִ֔י וְתַחֲלִימֵ֖נִי וְהַחֲיֵֽנִי׃

passages.text: Surely for my own welfare I had such great anguish; but Your love has delivered me from the pit of oblivion, for You have cast all my sins behind Your back.
passages.sermon:
God is the one who saves and forgives.
I suffered great anguish for my own good.
I felt deep bitterness.
But You, God, loved me.
You rescued my life from the pit of destruction.
You threw all my sins behind Your back.
You did not remember my sins anymore.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֥ה לְשָׁל֖וֹם מַר־ לִ֣י מָ֑ר וְאַתָּ֞ה חָשַׁ֤קְתָּ נַפְשִׁי֙ מִשַּׁ֣חַת בְּלִ֔י כִּ֥י הִשְׁלַ֛כְתָּ אַחֲרֵ֥י גֵוְךָ֖ כָּל־ חֲטָאָֽי׃

passages.text: For Sheol cannot thank You; Death cannot praise You. Those who descend to the Pit cannot hope for Your faithfulness.
passages.sermon:
Sheol is the place of the dead.
Sheol cannot thank You, Lord.
Death cannot praise You, Lord.
People who go down to the Pit cannot hope for Your faithfulness.
The dead cannot trust in Your truth.
passages.original: כִּ֣י לֹ֥א שְׁא֛וֹל תּוֹדֶ֖ךָּ מָ֣וֶת יְהַלְלֶ֑ךָּ לֹֽא־ יְשַׂבְּר֥וּ יֽוֹרְדֵי־ ב֖וֹר אֶל־ אֲמִתֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: The living, only the living, can thank You, as I do today; fathers will tell their children about Your faithfulness.
passages.sermon:
The living person can thank You.
Only the living can praise You.
I am alive today.
I thank You now.
A father will tell his children about Your faithfulness.
Fathers teach their children that You are faithful.
passages.original: חַ֥י חַ֛י ה֥וּא יוֹדֶ֖ךָ כָּמ֣וֹנִי הַיּ֑וֹם אָ֣ב לְבָנִ֔ים יוֹדִ֖יעַ אֶל־ אֲמִתֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: The LORD will save me; we will play songs on stringed instruments all the days of our lives in the house of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD will save me.
We will play songs on stringed instruments.
We will do this all the days of our lives.
We will play these songs in the house of the LORD.
passages.original: יְהוָ֖ה לְהוֹשִׁיעֵ֑נִי וּנְגִנוֹתַ֧י נְנַגֵּ֛ן כָּל־ יְמֵ֥י חַיֵּ֖ינוּ עַל־ בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Now Isaiah had said, “Prepare a lump of pressed figs and apply it to the boil, and he will recover.”
passages.sermon:
Isaiah was a prophet of God.
Isaiah spoke to the people.
Isaiah gave a command.
He said, “Take a lump of pressed figs.”
He said, “Apply the figs to the boil.”
He said, “He will recover.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְשַׁעְיָ֔הוּ יִשְׂא֖וּ דְּבֶ֣לֶת תְּאֵנִ֑ים וְיִמְרְח֥וּ עַֽל־ הַשְּׁחִ֖ין וְיֶֽחִי׃

passages.text: And Hezekiah had asked, “What will be the sign that I will go up to the house of the LORD?”
passages.sermon:
Hezekiah was the king of Judah.
Hezekiah spoke.
Hezekiah asked a question.
Hezekiah said, “What will be the sign?”
Hezekiah wanted a sign from God.
Hezekiah wanted to know when he would go up to the house of the LORD.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר חִזְקִיָּ֖הוּ מָ֣ה א֑וֹת כִּ֥י אֶעֱלֶ֖ה בֵּ֥ית יְהוָֽה׃ס
